hyps.why: Raising an already large learning rate (0.08-1) drives Adam into divergence, so the edit hurts much more there.
At tiny learning rates training is too slow to converge in 243 epochs, so increasing the rate helps most.
Lowering an unstable learning rate recovers accuracy, whereas lowering an already small one slows training.
Large batches give fewer, less noisy updates, so they tolerate and benefit from larger step sizes.
With a small learning rate, larger batches reduce the number of updates and worsen underfitting.
More updates per epoch from smaller batches compensate for a too-small learning rate.
At large alpha the L2 penalty dominates, so increasing it further collapses the model toward underfitting.
Relaxing a crushing L2 penalty restores capacity, while lowering a negligible alpha does nothing.
Adding units to a very narrow network fixes a capacity bottleneck, with diminishing returns once the network is wide.
Deeper networks are more sensitive to large steps, so adding layers worsens high-learning-rate instability.
